A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMedAgent-RL. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original medical VQA evaluations, component ablations, specialist comparisons, triage results, and case studies.

after.justification: V3 reports original medical VQA results and expanded experiments on routing, aggregation, test-time scaling, specialist composition, and backbone transfer.

M1.justification: V1 uses three-stage curriculum training with GRPO and stage-specific KL penalties. V3 adds an explicit entropy bonus with difficulty-dependent coefficients to the training objective, implemented in Equation 3.1 and Algorithm 1. This changes optimization beyond renaming C-MARL; the underlying GP-specialist-GP architecture remains.

E1.justification: Both versions train on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA and evaluate additionally on OmniMedVQA and MMMU Health & Medicine. V3's targeted hard-sample analysis revisits specialist-failure conditions already examined in v1; new model configurations and controls do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated MedVLThinker-7B and AFlow baselines, majority-voting and self-consistency variants, reasoning-based SFT controls, and trained SFT/GRPO aggregators. These substantially expand v1's comparisons. The detailed modality and MMMU tables also omit v1's GPT-4o-to-Qwen-3B and corresponding SFT comparator rows.

E3.justification: V3 shifts the main ablations from the 3B configuration to 7B and uses three o3 specialists for its principal reported configuration instead of GPT-4o. Added protocols include three-sample voting, targeted sets of 200 hard examples per dataset, simultaneous GP updates, and an InternVL2.5-8B backbone evaluation. Benchmark counts and the accuracy metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component, specialist, difficulty, triage, and KL analyses, v3 adds controls testing correction when every specialist fails, random routing, SFT versus GRPO triage, progressive component addition, independent versus simultaneous GP updates, backbone transfer, and trained aggregation. These investigate substantially more alternative explanations for the results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's multiple inference samples support voting and aggregation rather than statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the 7B ID/OOD averages of 72.7/67.7 in v1 with 73.3/72.6 in v3 under the revised method and specialist configuration; these are not identical-setting gains. V3 adds numerous results, including test-time-scaling averages of 76.1/76.6 and hard-subset accuracies of 26.5% on PathVQA and 23.0% on OmniMedVQA.

T1.justification: V1 contains algorithmic equations but no comparable convergence analysis. V3 introduces Section 4 and Appendix B, with distributional and loss assumptions, estimation and optimization bounds, and proofs comparing curriculum training with pooled-data SGD. Theorem 4.1 and Theorems B.1-B.2 are substantive additions.

C1.justification: The central claims about RL-optimized medical-agent collaboration and generalization remain. V3 adds dynamic entropy regulation to the advertised contribution, changes the headline claimed gain from 18.4% over SFT to 23.6% over strong baselines, and drops the introduction's claim that the 3B model rivals a 7B model.

C2.justification: V3 develops an entropy-based exploration-exploitation explanation beyond v1's imitation-to-correction account. It also interprets hard-case success as synthesis of useful fragments from incorrect specialist reasoning, explains curriculum optimization through successive warm starts, and argues for model-independent applicability and the efficiency of decoupled GP training.

D1.justification: Most of v1's training recipe, hardware, data counts, and prompt remain. V3 specifies entropy coefficients, names vLLM for inference, describes offline specialist-trajectory generation, and clarifies that difficulty labels are unavailable during inference. It also documents new baseline sampling and distillation details, while removing the explicit DeepSpeed ZeRO2/ZeRO3 configurations.

R1.justification: V3 broadens the research context to entropy-based RL, optimization theory, clinical-agent evaluation, and newer medical RL systems. New references include Cui and Wang on entropy, AI Hospital, AgentClinic, DoctorAgent-RL, and Med-U1. It removes several earlier generic-agent and specialty-model references, including the XrayGPT, PathChat, and OphGLM discussion.

P1.justification: The original narrative order and much of the exposition remain recognizable. V3 revises selected introduction and methodology passages, shortens the conclusion, inserts a theory section, and extends the appendix organization. It also adds ethics, reproducibility, and language-model-use statements and updates author and conference-header text.

P2.justification: V3 revises the framework diagram to show entropy regulation, removes v1's Figure 3 motivation graphic, expands the specialist chart, and adds numerous analytical tables. Main tables gain colored highlighting and improvement annotations. The main case display contracts from four examples to two, while the seven appendix cases are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added routing, trained-aggregator, hard-case, and backbone controls make v3's empirical support more informative than v1's, and implementation disclosures improve clarity. However, stronger o3 specialists complicate attribution of the headline gains. New reporting defects also limit the benefit: Table 5 reports 62.4 as the average of 60.9 and 57.8, and Theorem B.1 states an error bound four times tighter than its proof establishes. The additional evidence supports a limited net improvement, rather than a substantial increase in reliability.
